title: Put PLINK 2 in bin/

blocks.what_we_do:
The project package already contains PLINK 2 Beta 1.4 for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Linux. A build is a version of the program made for one system and processor. R finds your system, copies the matching build into the `bin/` folder and checks that it is the right file. You do not download anything. Follow these actions:

1. Keep the project from step 0.4 open in RStudio.
2. Run the command below in the console.
3. Read the last line it prints. It should say that PLINK 2 is ready in `bin/`.

The program is `plink2.exe` on Windows and `plink2` on macOS or Linux. This file is the [executable](docs/glossary.md#executable), the file your computer can run. The builds are in `third_party/plink2/programs/`. R never changes a different PLINK 2 file that you put in `bin/` yourself. It tells you instead. If you cloned the project with Git, the builds are not in the clone. R then downloads the pinned build and checks it in the same way.

You can still get PLINK 2 from the official page, <https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink/2.0/>. Use it only if R cannot prepare the program, or if your lecturer asks for a different version. Choose the build whose name matches your system and processor from step 0.1. Extract the ZIP file and copy only `plink2.exe` (or `plink2`) into `bin/`. If you are not sure that your processor supports AVX2 (an instruction set of the processor), choose the 64-bit build without AVX2.
blocks.why: PLINK 2 reads the genotype file formats. It computes [quality control](docs/glossary.md#quality-control) (QC) and association statistics. QC means checks that find samples or data that cannot be trusted. PLINK 1.9 is a different program, so it does not replace PLINK 2. The course checks the file against a stored SHA-256 value, a fingerprint of the file. This shows that you have the exact program that the course was tested with. The tested version is stored in one place, the settings file `config.R`. The setup check at step 0.8 reports your version and warns you if it differs.
blocks.you_need: The extracted project from step 0.3 and the R session from step 0.5. Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit Intel or AMD), macOS, or Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.31 or newer. For Windows ARM or Linux ARM, ask support for a compatible version.
blocks.command:
```{r s0-6_plink, eval=FALSE}
# 1. Load the helper that prepares PLINK 2.
source("R/plink_setup.R")
# 2. Copy the PLINK 2 build for your computer into the bin folder and check it.
prepare_course_plink()
```

Run this command yourself; the whole-path script omits it. It finishes in a few seconds.
blocks.expected_result: R prints one line. On the first run it is `PLINK 2 2.0.0-b.1.4 is ready in bin/ (windows-x86_64, from the package).` The system name in brackets matches your computer. If the file is already there, R prints `The course PLINK 2 program is already in bin/ and has the expected version.` The folder `bin` now holds `plink2.exe` on Windows, or `plink2` on macOS or Linux.
blocks.troubleshooting:
If R says that your computer cannot use the programs of the course, download PLINK 2 yourself from the official page, as described above. For Windows ARM or Linux ARM, ask support.

On macOS, Gatekeeper may block the program. Open a terminal in the project folder and type `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine bin/plink2`. This command removes the quarantine mark that macOS adds to downloaded files. You can also open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, find the message for `plink2` and click "Open Anyway". Follow [Apple's instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445). Then run step 0.6 again.

On Linux, PLINK 2 needs glibc 2.31 or newer. If you see the message "Kernel too old" or a glibc error, your system is too old for this build. Ask support. If the file lacks permission to run, type `chmod u+x bin/plink2` in the project folder.

On Windows, SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC". Review "More info" and use "Run anyway" if your institution permits it. If that option is unavailable, ask support. See [Microsoft's SmartScreen guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/smartscreen-reputation).

If R says that a SHA-256 value does not match, do not use the file. Download the project package again, or ask the instructor.
blocks.quick_check:
Does the command at step 0.6 download PLINK 2 from the internet?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. It copies the build that is already in the project package. Only if the package has no build for your system does it download the pinned build, and it checks the SHA-256 value first.</details>

student_summary: We prepare PLINK 2, the program that analyses the DNA data. The project already contains it, so R copies the right version for your computer into the bin folder and checks it.

If the file is already there, R prints `The course PLINK 2 program is already in bin/ and has the expected version.` The folder `bin` now holds `plink2.exe` on Windows, or `plink2` on macOS or Linux.
